distinguishing_features: Localized laser shock peening of the axle wheel-seat fillet to create a compressive residual-stress layer.
Fatigue resistance is sought by altering the local stress state without changing the axle geometry.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce fatigue-crack initiation at the wheel-seat fillet while retaining the axle geometry.
parsed.viable_reason: As written, a 10 µs pulse is far too long for effective laser shock peening, and the specified setup does not establish the required shock-confinement arrangement, so the claimed compressive layer cannot be relied upon.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the supplied prior arts teaches or suggests localized residual-stress treatment of an axle fillet; their monitoring and operating-control mechanisms do not lead to this treatment.
